# Kition kit rules (read first)

<!-- kition-quality:begin (generated by kition-sdk tools/sync-quality.mjs; edit the template there) -->
## Quality rules (read first)

- Tests are the spec. Read `docs/quality.md` and the feature catalogue (`features.yaml`)
  before changing behaviour. When code and a case disagree, the case wins unless a maintainer
  approves changing the case.
- Before you finish any task, run `cargo fmt --all -- --check`. If it fails, the task is not done. Claude Code
  runs it for you through the Stop hook; agents without hooks (Codex) run it by hand and
  report the real exit code.
- The full checks and tests run on GitHub, in the kit's CI run, not on your machine: a task is
  done only when HEAD has a passing CI run and is on `origin/main`. Use Kition's
  `scripts/kit-ci.sh` (`push`, `wait`, `failures`, `land`; Kition's `docs/kits.md`, section
  4c). Compile only the crates you touched locally.
- Never edit expected results to make a test pass: files under `cases/**/expected/`, paths
  listed under `protected` in `features.yaml`, and the `expected`, `tolerance`, `reference`,
  `input` and `steps` of an existing `case.yaml`. If you believe an expected result is wrong,
  stop and explain why in the task's findings; only a maintainer approves expected-result changes.
- Never weaken a test to make it pass: no deleted or loosened assertions, no added
  `#[ignore]`, `.skip`, `.only` or `.todo`, no raised tolerances. kition-sdk's
  `tools/check-expected.mjs` lists every such change for the maintainers.
- Every bug fix starts with a failing case under `cases/regressions/issue-<n>/`, then the fix.
- Every new feature adds an entry to `features.yaml` and at least one gating test.
- Put the task id and the case ids in the commit message.
- Stage only your own files: `git add` them by name; never `git commit -a` or `git add -A`.
  Other sessions may have uncommitted work in the same checkout.
- Work on `kition-slide` only in its main checkout; never change, build, or commit in its worktrees (`kition-slide-wt/*`, `kition-*-wt`, `kition-naming-work`).
- Never start `cargo xtask eval` (the real-model `layer: eval` cases): only a maintainer starts it (F-QA-16). Write eval cases and check them with `--dry-run`, which calls no model.
- No compatibility layers: no aliases, old names, old file suffixes, migrations, or readers for
  old formats. Delete a replaced path in the same change.
<!-- kition-quality:end -->

This repository is Kition's `kit.film` kit, not the upstream editor it started from. These rules
come first; the upstream rules below still apply to the engine.

- The kit draws **its own editor**: `web/` is a React app on `@kition/sdk/editor` (kition-sdk's
  shared kit UI library) with Kition Film's menu bar, the program monitor, the transport, and the track timeline; a host (Kition, or `web/dev.html` for development) shows it
  in an iframe and talks to it over the Kit UI protocol (`kition-kit-ui/1`, kition-sdk `docs/platform/reference/ui-protocol.md`). Style it only with the host's theme tokens and kit-editor components;
  ribbon labels and command titles are the upstream editor's English text, translated by its
  catalogs in `web/src/i18n/upstream/` and, where those lack a label, by `PHRASES` in
  `web/src/strings.ts` (with the editor's own `en-US` and `zh-CN` strings). Chinese has its own
  catalog, `web/src/i18n/upstream/zh-hans.tsv`: every label the editor draws gets an entry there (or
  in `zh-CN` for its own strings) in the same change, which `pnpm --dir web test:parity` and the flow
  test check. A new table or const of labels drawn through a variable (`phrase(TABLE[key])`, a
  message passed to `status`) is registered in `LABEL_TABLES` in `web/parity/i18n.mjs`, so the
  check reads it. Engine and error text goes to the status bar through `errorStatus`, not `status`. Files go only through the host.
- `bindings/wasm` compiles the engine to WebAssembly on the public `KitionAI/kition-sdk`
  crate; the editor runs it in a Web Worker. The contract and the Kition platform rules live in kition-sdk
  (`docs/platform/kits/engine.md`, `docs/platform/reference/ui-protocol.md`), the agent protocol
  in KHP (`kitharness/kitharness`, https://github.com/kitharness/kitharness);
  change them there, never here.
  `kition-film-kit` must keep passing `kition_kit::testing::check_contract`.
- Media are read only through `kition_kit::host` (lent files): synchronous ranged reads the host
  serves from the workspace. Never read the filesystem directly in the SDK, never load a whole
  video, and treat a missing file as an ordinary error ("media offline").
- The whole repository is Apache-2.0 ([LICENSE](LICENSE)); third-party notices are listed in
  `NOTICE`. Upstream is credited only in NOTICE; never write upstream names anywhere else.

# Kition Film — rules for agents and contributors

These rules apply to every human and AI contributor. `.claude/CLAUDE.md` holds the working instructions; this
file holds the rules that must never be broken. When the two disagree, this file wins.

## 0. Never crash

People trust Kition Film with hours of work. A malformed file, a bad command or MCP parameter, a corrupt
preset or project, an odd keystroke or a full disk must give an error the user (or agent) can act on,
never a crash and never lost work. **This rule outranks feature work:** don't ship a feature by adding a
panic path, and fix a crash before building on top of it.

1. **Fail with `Result<T, E>`.** Return the crate's error type and propagate with `?`; add context
   (`map_err`, an error variant) instead of discarding it. In the UI, report the error (status bar, error
   dialog) and carry on.
2. **No panicking shortcuts outside tests:** no `unwrap()`, `expect()`, `panic!`, `unreachable!`, `todo!`
   or `unimplemented!`. Use `?`, `ok_or(..)?`, `let Some(x) = .. else { return Err(..) }`, `if let`, or a
   fallback that is truly correct (never one that silently corrupts a project). An unfinished feature
   returns an "unsupported" error. The only exception is a call that is provably infallible from local
   code alone (a literal that always parses): a single-item `#[allow(clippy::expect_used)]` with the reason.
3. **No `unsafe`** (`unsafe_code = "forbid"` for the whole workspace, with no exception).
4. **Every input-derived number is hostile.** Media files, project and interchange files, presets, fonts,
   CLI / MCP / control-channel parameters and UI state are untrusted. Index and slice with `get()` (or
   validate bounds once, up front, for a hot loop); slice strings only at char boundaries; use
   `checked_*` / `saturating_*` for lengths, offsets and counts; never divide by a value that can be zero
   (frame rates, timescales, sample rates, sizes); don't cast negative or NaN values to integers; don't
   call `clamp` with bounds that can cross; cap allocations sized by input.
5. **Bound recursion and loops.** Projects can be cyclic (nested sequences) or deeply nested: walk them
   with seen-sets or depth limits.
6. **Don't cascade.** Lock poisoning is not fatal: `lock().unwrap_or_else(PoisonError::into_inner)`.
   Every thread or job (export, previews, proxies, decoding workers…) runs under `catch_unwind` and
   reports a failure as an error: a dead worker leaves monitors blank or jobs "running" forever.
7. **No last-resort guard.** This kit has no panic hook and no `catch_unwind` wrapper around the
   editor. Rules 1–6 are the only defense against a crash here.
8. **Prove it.** Every crash fix comes with a small synthetic regression test that panicked before the
   fix. Parsers and decoders get mutation-fuzz tests (truncation, bit flips, corrupt sizes) run under
   `catch_unwind`; new commands get hostile-parameter tests. Fuzzer findings become tests.
9. **Enforced:** clean crates carry `#![deny(clippy::unwrap_used, clippy::expect_used, clippy::panic,
   clippy::unimplemented, clippy::todo, clippy::unreachable)]` (moving to `[workspace.lints.clippy]` once
   every crate is clean). `.clippy.toml` allows them in tests: a failing test should fail loudly.

## 1. Assets: no Adobe artwork, every asset licensed and attributed

This rule is absolute. Breaking it is the most serious mistake a contributor can make on this project.

**What counts as an asset:** any image, icon, cursor, logo, illustration, screenshot, font, colour LUT,
preset, template, sound, music, video, 3D model, or other non-code media. This covers files in the
repository, bytes embedded in code (`include_bytes!`, base64, data URIs), and data hard-coded to
reproduce an image (for example, point lists traced from someone else's icon).

1. **Never use Adobe iconography, images or other Adobe assets**, in any form:
   - no icons, cursors, logos, splash screens, UI artwork or screenshots from any Adobe product;
   - no Adobe fonts, LUTs, presets, templates, sound effects, stock media or sample projects;
   - no traced, redrawn, recoloured or "inspired-by" copies of Adobe icons. Our icons may follow generic
     conventions (a play triangle, a razor blade, a stopwatch), but each must be drawn from scratch
     without reference to Adobe's artwork.
2. **Every asset must be open**: open-source licensed (MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD, ISC, zlib, SIL OFL…),
   public domain / CC0, or Creative Commons (CC BY or CC BY-SA; no NC/ND licenses), **or** created by a
   contributor who owns it and licenses it to the project under the project license (Apache-2.0).
   If the license is unknown or unclear, the asset does not go in.
3. **Every asset needs an attribution sidecar.** Next to each asset file `X`, add `X.attribution` with:
   ```text
   asset:        <file name>
   title:        <what it is>
   author:       <creator / copyright holder>
   source:       <URL, or "original work" for contributor-made assets>
   license:      <SPDX id or license name>
   license-file: <path to the license text, if the license requires shipping it>
   added:        <YYYY-MM-DD> by <contributor>
   notes:        <how it was made or modified; for screenshots, what is shown>
   ```
   Also add one line for the asset to [`docs/attribution.md`](docs/attribution.md). `cargo xtask assets` (part of
   `cargo xtask ci`) fails if any asset lacks a sidecar or index entry.
4. **Screenshots** in the repo may show only Kition Film (or other open projects), with media we generated
   or media that is itself openly licensed. Never commit screenshots of Adobe products.
5. **Local reference material stays local.** Premiere reference screenshots and notes live only in
   `plan/premiere/` (gitignored). They must never be committed, bundled, embedded, traced or shipped.
6. **Code-drawn assets** (procedural demo footage in `crates/media/media`, procedural looks in
   `crates/render/render`) are original work under the project license and are listed in
   `docs/attribution.md`.
7. **When in doubt, leave it out** and draw or generate it yourself.
8. **Fonts live in [KitionAI/kition-fonts](https://github.com/KitionAI/kition-fonts), never in this
   repo.** Don't commit new font files (the small Latin UI fonts already in `assets/fonts/` stay). A
   font Kition Film needs is added to kition-fonts, which the app reads through the optional build input
   `KITION_FONTS_DIR=<absolute path of a kition-fonts checkout>` (`crates/support/text/build.rs` embeds the fonts in its
   `fonts/manifest.txt` as `kition_film_text::fonts::KITION_FONTS`; unset, it is empty and the app uses its
   bundled and system fonts). Never add kition-fonts to a `Cargo.toml`. Code using `KITION_FONTS` must work
   when it is empty.

## 2. Clean-room code

- Never read, disassemble or copy anything inside Adobe application bundles; file names and listings only.
  Observe behaviour by using the app; never capture its Home screen, recent projects, account info or
  file browsers.
- Never copy GPL/LGPL/AGPL code (FFmpeg, x264, x265, MLT, Kdenlive, Shotcut, Olive, LAME…).
- Implement codecs and formats from public specifications (ITU-T/ISO/IEC standards, IETF RFCs, the VP9
  and AV1 bitstream specs, SMPTE documents, published container specs). Do not read the source of
  reference or third-party decoders/encoders while implementing a format, even permissively licensed
  ones (libvpx, libopus, libaom, dav1d, openh264…); spec text and conformance vectors only. Record the
  spec edition used in the crate README.
- ffmpeg/ffprobe may be used only as external test oracles and fixture generators. They are never
  linked, bundled or shipped.
- Dependencies must use permissive licenses: MIT/Apache-2.0/BSD/ISC/Zlib/Unicode/CC0/BSL-1.0, or
  MPL-2.0 used unmodified.

## 3. Engineering rules

### 3.1 Never crash

See [§0](#0-never-crash). It outranks every other engineering rule.

### 3.2 The rest

See `.claude/CLAUDE.md`: pure Rust, dependency layering (`cargo xtask layers`), exact `Tick` time, everything is
a command, everything is agent-drivable, and the quality gates (`cargo xtask ci`) before every commit.


Shared real-file test corpora (Photoshop-authored PSDs, etc.) live in
[`KitionAI/kition-photo-corpus`](https://github.com/KitionAI/kition-photo-corpus). Never commit
large binary fixtures to this repo; fetch them pinned by commit and sha256-verified, as Kition
Photo does with `cargo xtask corpus`.
